title: Generated catalogue requests: does the record satisfy every constraint?
decision: whether a catalogue record satisfies every constraint of a request (yes) or violates one of them by at most one step of the quantity it compares (no)

source.name: generator build/gen_filter_match.py
source.version: gen_v4, 2026-10-08: day-count convention stated in every request that counts days; field wording that cannot be read as another field; plausible records (list price >= price, bundle at 0.70-0.95 of the unit price, price and physical specs inside per-category ranges); meta.level 1/2/3 = 6/9/12 constraints (script of 2026-10-07, harder dials v2; DIFFICULTY = "v1" regenerates the first version)

licence: generated by the benchmark's script (no third-party text)
notes: Version v2 (harder than the first version, which is regenerated with DIFFICULTY = "v1"). 600 items = 300 contrast pairs (meta.pair, group): one request with a record that satisfies all constraints (yes) and the same record with one field changed so that exactly one constraint fails (no). The compared quantity of the planted constraint is ON the limit named in the request or ONE step from it in both members of a pair (a step is one cent, one gram, one day, one certification, ...): in the negative on the limit (a wording that does not count it) or one step beyond it, in the positive on the limit (a wording that counts it) or one step inside it. Dial: constraints (6, 9, 12), twenty kinds of which ten need a small computation on the record (price per unit, discount from the list price, price plus shipping, a unit conversion with the factor stated, days between two dates, a date plus days, the age of the listing on a stated day, at least k of n certifications, a delivery limit that only applies to items shipped from outside a region); meta.margin and meta.pattern say how the planted constraint sits to its limit. The metric is item accuracy; the group allows a pair analysis. Everything is invented and every answer is computed twice (specification and a parser of the rendered request); the README lists the ten computed kinds with the step of each. State length 1157 to 2024 characters (median 1621). gen_v4 (2026-10-08): a request that counts days says how (the difference between the two dates, the same day is 0 days; a date plus N days is N days later), no wording can be read as another field of the record (the maker is only 'made by', a region only 'ships to'), the records are plausible (list price above the price, a bundle at 0.70 to 0.95 of the unit price, the price and every physical spec inside the range of its category, the width below the length) and meta.level is 1 / 2 / 3 for 6 / 9 / 12 constraints.

sample.note: a sample of two whole contrast groups (one of level 1, one of level 3) for the tests of this repository; EVALUATION ONLY, never a training source
